field.label: Clues: a device must match all of them
MAC vendor
field.help: A whole word of the maker's name, e.g. Tuya. Separate several with commas: any of them matches.

field.label: Host name
field.help: Its DHCP or Bonjour host name, a regular expression, e.g. ^kvm-[0-9a-f]{4}$

field.label: Bonjour model
field.help: A model it announces over Bonjour, a regular expression, e.g. ^AppleTV

field.label: Bonjour service
field.help: A service it announces, exactly, e.g. _hap._tcp. Separate several with commas: any of them matches.

field.label: DHCP vendor class
field.help: The vendor class in its DHCP request, a regular expression, e.g. ^udhcp

field.label: Talks to
field.help: A domain it uses, including its subdomains, e.g. nordvpn.com. Separate several with commas: any of them matches.

field.label: MAC prefix
field.help: The start of its MAC address, e.g. 52:54:00. Separate several with commas: any of them matches.

field.label: MAC address
field.help: Phones, tablets and laptops usually use a private (randomized) address on each network.

field.label: Type
field.help: The device type to show, e.g. Window shade. Your rules are checked before the built-in ones; an override for one device still wins.

field.label: Icon
field.help: Shown next to the type. Automatic uses the icon of a built-in type with the same name.
